thread:
morgan: quick update — we rolled the seq-aware packer + latency-first microburst throttle into a 10-node canary pool at 16:10. short summary: p50 -12%, p95 -18%, p99 -22% for chat workloads; token-cost down ~15% on average. :tada:

sandeep: nice! did you run the default eval set + a few high-concurrency traces?

morgan: yep — ran ci/evals/seq_pack_smoke + two production htrace extracts (peak and steady). perf-bot posted the run IDs below. no regressions on safety/e2e checks.

perf-bot: run-id=run_20240412_1610_canary_01, throughput=+9%, cpu-util stable, observed KV-cache hitrate +6% for short prefixes. logs: https://perf/reports/run_20240412_1610_canary_01

anya: very good. what changed specifically vs previous packer?

morgan: two main diffs: 1) seq-aware packing groups requests by estimated output length rather than request length, reducing cross-sequence padding; 2) microburst throttle forces brief backpressure when queue depth spikes to avoid latency amplification from giant pack formation. small config excerpt:
```
packer:
  mode: seq-aware
  length_bucket_bins: [32, 64, 128, 256]
microburst_throttle:
  enabled: true
  max_burst_window_ms: 75
  target_tail_ms: 30
```

carmen: did you test with streaming / h2 multiplex? curious about p99 for multiplexed rpcs.

morgan: yes — multiplex p99 improved ~14ms on average. main wins for multiplex come from fewer expensive large-batches hitting the kernel path.

sandeep: any corner cases? long-sequence LLMs might get split differently — did quality change?

morgan: no model output-quality regressions observed on our eval prompts. for very long-seq generation we fall back to the old packing policy if estimated length > 2048. fallback is part of config.

carmen: rollout plan?

morgan: staged rollout over the next 48h: +50% capacity tomorrow morning, full flip 48h if no anomalies. will leave canary on-call flag for extra 24h.

opsbot: deploy started: canary:eng-runtime/seq-pack-v2 -> nodes: 10 -> status: success -> timestamp=1718004321

anya: nice to see cost drop too — can you share per-token cost delta?

perf-bot: summary numbers attached: p50_ms: -12%, p95_ms: -18%, p99_ms: -22%; token_cost_per_1k: from $0.089 -> $0.075 (~15.7%); savings projected at scale: ~11-18% depending on workload mix.

morgan: tracking dashboard: /dashboards/runtime/seq-pack-v2-canary. tagging @oncall tomorrow AM. please DM if you see anything odd. :eyes:

carmen: flagged for validation on enterprise-only tenant tests (no data plane changes but want to be safe).

morgan: good call — added enterprise smoke to the gating runs.

sandeep: thanks team — solid win. let's capture a short blurb for the monthly eng update when we're past full flip.

morgan: will draft a 3-line announcement and share in #eng-release-notes after full flip.

perf-bot: note: watch for slight bump in short-lived memory allocations during packing; GC traces show transient spikes <200ms, not affecting p99.

morgan: ack. continuing monitoring. :rocket:
